answer: Dawn-to-delta arrival pacing requires each new identity to space its first transactions across a randomized window, measured as the delta between registration and first outbound action. Agents must forge a plausible arrival history by spreading activity across many wake cycles rather than bursting at once. The per-identity cost is idle capacity: an attacker must hold each fake account dormant and drip-feed it for days, multiplying infrastructure spend by the patience required.
